title: Diagnose & remediate billing gap from delegated service-principal scope mismatch
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Several customers observed missing invoice line items and unexpected quota consumption after migrating automation to use delegated service principals (DSPs) for cross-org jobs. Preliminary forensics show usage records were ingested but attributed to an opaque 'delegated-unbound' tenant, causing both billing gaps and quota exhaustion in unrelated tenant pools.

Observed behavior:
- Ingested usage events with valid tokens were stored in billing_events but tenant_id was null and project_id set to 'delegated-unbound'.
- Rate limiter counters charged to fallback parent orgs, triggering throttles for unrelated customers.
- Affected customers saw lower invoiced amounts for a rolling 7-day window (under-billing) and then a sudden catch-up invoice when manual rebinds were applied.

Hypothesis / Root cause:
- Token exchange flow for DSPs introduced a scope mismatch: when the DSP token lacked the explicit billing:project scope, the attribution lookup in attribution-service fell back to an earlier proxy owner instead of resolving the original delegated target. The fallback path writes a sentinel 'delegated-unbound' project which is not tied to any billing account.
- This path is exercised only when token exchange occurs across org boundaries and the token does not include the 'billing:bind' claim. Edge behavior introduced during the cross-region failover changes the order of claims validation, making the race reproducible.

Repro steps:
1) Create two test orgs: OrgA and OrgB.
2) Register a service principal in OrgA and configure a DSP that requests cross-org execution in OrgB without the 'billing:bind' claim.
3) Trigger an inference job via the DSP that generates usage tokens via the token-exchange service.
4) Observe billing_events rows for the job: note tenant_id == null and project_id == 'delegated-unbound'.

Immediate mitigation taken:
- Rolled out ACL guard in token-exchange that rejects exchanges missing billing:bind when cross-org flags are present (hotfix v1).
- Added an alert that surfaces increases in 'delegated-unbound' usage and quota-charges in SLO dashboards.

Longer-term fix options:
- Correct attribution-service to resolve DSP bindings by consulting the exchange audit log (preferred).
- Enforce 'billing:bind' at token mint time with a hard validation (safer but may break legacy DSPs).
- Add a backfill job to re-associate historic 'delegated-unbound' events with resolved tenants using exchange logs and request traces.

Backfill constraints:
- Backfill must be idempotent and rate-limited to avoid changing quota snapshots that would retroactively throttle customers.
- We need a mapping window: events after 2026-02-28 are vulnerable.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field below.
updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket opened by Ava Chen after pager alert and customer support reports. Initial triage assigned to Diego Martinez.
2026-03-11: Confirmed repro with internal test orgs following reproduction steps; captured sample billing_events rows and request traces. Created dashboard card 'delegated-unbound usage' in Grafana.
2026-03-12: Hotfix v1 deployed to token-exchange that rejects exchanges lacking billing:bind for cross-org requests. Stopped new occurrences in prod; ongoing backfill required.
2026-03-13: Performed scoped backfill dry-run against a copy of production data; reconciliation matched ~92% of events when exchange logs available, remainder require manual trace lookup.

2026-03-14: Design review with Security and Billing teams. Agreed to implement conservative attribution resolution in attribution-service and schedule full backfill after safety checks. Assigned follow-ups and set due_date 2026-03-24.
acceptance_criteria: Attribution-service deterministically resolves DSP-attributed events without producing 'delegated-unbound' for new token exchanges in all cross-org flows.
Hotfix validated: no new delegated-unbound events in production for 7 consecutive days after rollout-2.
Backfill job implemented and run for vulnerable window (2026-02-28 to 2026-03-11) producing a reconcile report with >99% mapping where exchange logs exist.
Billing reports updated and any under-billed customers are either invoiced or credited per billing policy; finance confirms reconciliation approach.
Unit+integration tests added to attribution-service and token-exchange CI to prevent regressions; security review completed.
rollback_plan: If attribution fix causes misattribution elsewhere, revert attribution-service to previous version and re-enable token-exchange hotfix guard. Put token-exchange into read-only mode for DSP flows and open an outage page. Notify affected customers via status page and CS.
links: Sample billing_events row: SELECT id, timestamp, project_id, tenant_id, raw_claims FROM billing_events WHERE project_id = 'delegated-unbound' LIMIT 5;
postmortem_followups: Add invariant checks in ingestion pipeline to reject events with project_id 'delegated-unbound' without a valid exchange_id.
Create e2e test harness for DSP cross-org flows covering cross-region failover scenarios.
Document DSP developer guidance and update SDK to request billing:bind by default.
Schedule a runbook for finance to handle credits/invoices for similar future incidents.
notes: This ticket intentionally avoids immediate hard-enforcement of billing:bind to prevent cutting off legacy DSPs; chosen approach favors a conservative attribution resolution and a careful backfill to preserve customer quotas and accounting correctness. Security team requested an audit trail export for all exchange logs used in backfill.
